findings.title: A null identity entry is rewritten to `{}`, turning a removal into an assignment.
findings.body:
`clean_null_values(properties) or {}` maps every entry to at least `{}`, including entries whose value is `null`. In ARM managed-identity PATCH semantics, `"<id>": null` means "unassign this identity", while `{}` means "assign it".

Trigger: a manifest passed to `update --yaml` that lists one identity as `null` and keeps another.
- Before this change, the null entry was dropped. The map sent no longer contained that identity, so it was effectively removed.
- Now it is sent as `{}`, so the identity the user meant to remove stays assigned (or gets assigned).

Only `{}` (or dicts that clean to `{}`) should be kept. Drop entries whose original value is `None`, for example:
`{i: clean_null_values(p) or {} for i, p in value.items() if p is not None}`.
Alternatively, pass `None` through unchanged if sending explicit removals is wanted.
